claim_boundary: This proof counts one internally reproduced March 2020 BLS PPI boundary because two pre-decision final-demand release records, four exact official HTML/PDF hashes, exact 8:30 a.m. EDT embargo timing, paired-format and adjacent-release cross-checks, a separately locked May 13 April event, immutable locks, separated truth labels, an explicit March-change persistence baseline, a no-probability persistence-or-one-known-increase program, deliberate TrialCourt failure, deterministic outputs, limitations, and a clean-checkout double rebuild all verify. The April change of -130 basis points is excluded from ReplayPack inputs and used only for a labelled post-event check that preserves its 110-basis-point lower-bound breach rather than widening the -20-to-20 basis-point range. The March release preserves February at -60 basis points, and the May release preserves March at -20 basis points; those zero revisions do not convert the range into a forecast. PPI measures average changes in prices received by domestic producers from the seller perspective and is subject to revision four months after original publication. Unadjusted indexes, 12-month changes, and COVID-19 methodology text remain metadata and set no endpoint or causal conclusion. This proof does not establish a BLS forecast, calibrated coverage, consumer prices, product or establishment behavior, quantity, revenue, profit, transactions, price-setting, pass-through, pandemic or market causality, external validation, deployment, investment performance, or user impact.

deliberate_failure_modes.description: TrialCourt must reject the retrospective one-change attempt rather than promote it as a validated forecast.
The immutable trial ledger retains one rejected decision.

absence_reasons.observed: The lock contains aggregate seller-price changes reported in archived BLS releases, not producer, establishment, product, transaction, quantity, revenue, profit, consumer-price, causal, or future-event observations. The April change exists only in the disjoint event lock.

naive_baselines.description: The decision-time baseline persists the March final-demand monthly change of -20 basis points.
The persistence-or-one-known-increase endpoints carry no probability, confidence, or coverage claim.
Unadjusted indexes, 12-month changes, and release methodology text remain source metadata and set neither endpoint.
Both numeric inputs are headline values in archived BLS releases available by the April 9 decision boundary.
The later -130-basis-point April change never enters range construction.
